subject: Problem with exogenous and endogenous ordinal variables in model specification

messages.author: 3eb30cdcd09b506f
messages.subject: Problem with exogenous and endogenous ordinal variables in model specification
parts:
Hi there,

This is my R code:

modelqdvuni<-'
# measurement model 
perf=~Q13_1+Q13_2+Q13_3+Q13_4+Q13_5+perc_esami+Q8+Q9+Q10
ambiente=~Q14_1+Q14_2+Q14_3+Q14_4+Q14_5+Q14_7+Q13_1+Q13_3
qdvuni=~Q12_1+Q12_2+Q12_3+Q12_4+Q12_5+Q12_6+Q12_7+Q12_8+Q12_9+Q12_10+Q12_11+Q12_12

# regressions
qdvuni ~ perf + ambiente

# residual correlations
Q12_7 ~~ Q12_8 + Q12_6
Q12_5 ~~ Q12_8
Q12_3 ~~ Q12_2
Q12_12 ~~ Q12_11
'
fitqdvuni<-sem(modelqdvuni,data=data,ordered=c("Q8","Q10","Q14_1","Q14_2","Q14_3","Q14_4","Q14_5","Q14_7","Q13_1","Q13_2","Q13_3","Q13_4","Q12_1","Q12_2","Q12_3","Q12_4","Q12_5","Q12_6","Q12_7","Q12_8","Q12_9","Q12_10","Q12_11","Q12_12"))
summary(fitqdvuni,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE)

All observed variables except Q9 and perc_esami are ordinal.
The problem with the code above was about high values for goodness of fit indices (e.g. RMSEA).

I modified the code as follows, after having read this -> http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html (i.e. use ordered option just for endogenous categorical variables).

modelqdvuni<-'
# measurement model 
perf=~Q13_1+Q13_2+Q13_3+Q13_4+Q13_5+perc_esami+Q8+Q9+Q10
ambiente=~Q14_1+Q14_2+Q14_3+Q14_4+Q14_5+Q14_7+Q13_1+Q13_3
qdvuni=~Q12_1+Q12_2+Q12_3+Q12_4+Q12_5+Q12_6+Q12_7+Q12_8+Q12_9+Q12_10+Q12_11+Q12_12

# regressions
qdvuni ~ perf + ambiente

# residual correlations
Q12_7 ~~ Q12_8 + Q12_6
Q12_5 ~~ Q12_8
Q12_3 ~~ Q12_2
Q12_12 ~~ Q12_11
'
fitqdvuni<-sem(modelqdvuni,data=data,ordered=c("Q12_1","Q12_2","Q12_3","Q12_4","Q12_5","Q12_6","Q12_7","Q12_8","Q12_9","Q12_10","Q12_11","Q12_12"))
summary(fitqdvuni,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE)

I got smaller values for RMSEA, but am I correct?

Thank you.

Serena

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Problem with exogenous and endogenous ordinal variables in model specification
parts:
On 06/18/2015 11:06 AM, Serena Miccolis wrote:
> I mean am I correct in declaring as ordered ONLY the endogenous
> variables that are in the measurement model for the endogenous latent

> variable "/qdvuni/"? Or should I consider the categorical variables in
> the measurement model for the exogenous latent variables ("/perf"/ and
> "/ambiente"/) as well?

Yes. All indicators of latent variables are 'endogenous', and should be
declared as ordinal.

Yves.
